showOn.description:
Viewport-width breakpoint selector.  When set, the component subscribes to `window.matchMedia` and reactively shows/hides the content card whenever the viewport crosses the breakpoint.

Supported values: `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl` | `2xl` (Tailwind), or pixel expressions such as `>400px`, `>=640px`, `<768px`, `<=1024px`, `400px`.

When both `show` and `showOn` are provided the content is rendered only when **both** conditions are satisfied.

By default the breakpoint is evaluated against the **viewport** width via `window.matchMedia`.  Set `containerQuery: true` to evaluate it against the width of the **enclosing container** instead (uses `ResizeObserver`).

containerQuery.description:
When `true`, the `showOn` breakpoint is measured against the width of the component's **enclosing container** rather than the viewport.

Internally the component renders a transparent `<div style="width:100%">` wrapper and observes it with `ResizeObserver`.  This means a single extra DOM node is added when `containerQuery` is `true`.

Has no effect when `showOn` is not set.

keepMounted.description:
When `true`, the content card stays **mounted** even when the visibility condition is `false`.  Instead of returning `null`, the component wraps the card in a `<div style="display:none">` (hidden) or `<div style="display:contents">` (transparent pass-through when visible).

Use this for expensive subtrees — such as Plate editors — where remounting from scratch on every show/hide is too costly.

ConditionalProps.description:
Props for the `shad/conditional` card.

The card renders `content` only when the combined visibility condition is `true`; it renders nothing otherwise.  This is a transparent pass-through — no extra DOM wrapper is added.

## Modes

### 1 · Manual boolean (existing behaviour)

Drive `show` from a `memo()` selector so the card reactively mounts/unmounts as state changes:

```ts import {memo, registerCard} from "@pihanga2/core"; import {Conditional} from "@/cards/conditional";

registerCard("myApp/hint", Conditional({   show:    memo((s: AppState) => s.items.length === 0 && !s.isLoading),   content: "myApp/emptyStateHint", })); ```

### 2 · Breakpoint-based auto-selection (new)

Set `showOn` to a breakpoint name or pixel expression.  The component subscribes to `window.matchMedia` and automatically mounts/unmounts the content card as the viewport crosses the breakpoint — no state, no memo:

```ts // Show only on tablet-sized screens and up registerCard("myApp/sidebar", Conditional({   showOn:  "md",   content: "myApp/desktopSidebar", }));

// Show only on narrow viewports (mobile drawer) registerCard("myApp/mobileNav", Conditional({   showOn:  "<768px",   content: "myApp/drawer", })); ```

### 3 · Combined

Both conditions are ANDed — content renders only when the breakpoint matches
**and** `show` is `true`:

```ts registerCard("myApp/adminSidebar", Conditional({   show:    memo((s: AppState) => s.isAdmin),   showOn:  "lg",   content: "myApp/adminPanel", })); ```

Shows animated shimmer rows while `loading` is `true`; once `loading` becomes `false` it transparently passes through to `content` (or renders nothing when `content` is omitted).

**Quick setup** — use the preset props: ```ts registerCard("myApp/area", LoadingSkeleton({   loading:  memo((s: AppState) => s.dataLoading),   rows:     4,   rowSize:  "lg",   spacing:  "lg",   content:  "myApp/dataList", })); ```

**Custom Tailwind** — override with raw class strings: ```ts registerCard("myApp/area", LoadingSkeleton({   loading:      memo((s: AppState) => s.dataLoading),   rows:         4,   rowClassName: "h-32 rounded-xl bg-primary/10",   className:    "grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 w-full",   content:      "myApp/cardGrid", })); ```

- `"range"` – a vertical rectangle whose height is proportional to `extent`               in the content's scroll space, with a CSS-enforced minimum               height so tiny ranges remain clickable.  Requires `extent`.

formAction.description:
When set and this button is rendered inside a `pi/form` card, clicking it requests that top-level form action instead of firing this button's own `onClicked`:

- `"submit"` — same as pressing the form's native submit button; fires   the Form's `onSubmitted` event with a snapshot of the current field   values.
- `"cancel"` — fires the Form's `onCancelled` event. Never submits or   resets the form.

The button's native `<button type>` is derived from this prop so it can never accidentally submit a form it isn't supposed to: `"submit"` → `type="submit"`, `"cancel"` (or unset) → `type="button"`.

Has no effect when the button is used outside a `pi/form` — in that case `onClicked` always fires as usual, and the native type is `"button"`.

This is the button-specific counterpart of `FormFieldProps`/`name` used by form-bindable fields (`pi/input`, `pi/switch`, …) — together they form the complete `pi/form` interaction contract.

selfManaged.description:
**Standalone mode only** (ignored when used inside a `pi/form` card — see below). When true, the textarea keeps its own internal text state so the visible text always updates immediately as the user types, but the outgoing `onChanged` event is only dispatched at a "commit" point instead of on every keystroke:

 - always on blur,  - and, if `debounceMs > 0`, also after that many ms of typing    inactivity (a trailing debounce), so the value is committed even if    the user never blurs the field (e.g. drives an autosave / API call).

Use this to avoid flooding the host app / reducer with an event per keystroke for a card whose `onChanged` handler is expensive.

When the card is used inside a `pi/form` (i.e. `name` is set and a `pi/form` ancestor is present), this prop has no effect: form fields always write back to form state on every keystroke via `form.handleChange`, exactly like `pi/input` and `pi/text-field` — the form's own submit action is the natural "commit" point in that case.

Default: `false` (dispatches `onChanged` on every keystroke, as before).

debounceMs.description: Trailing-debounce window (ms) for committing changes while `selfManaged` is true (standalone mode only). `0` (default) means no debounce — the value is only committed on blur. Ignored when `selfManaged` is `false`, or when the card is inside a `pi/form`.

When `true`, the component manages its own selection state internally using `__imp_ReactValue__pihanga2_core`.  The `value` prop is used only as the initial value (i.e. `defaultValue`) and subsequent changes do not require an external state update.  `onChanged` is still fired so callers can observe changes without owning the state.

Has no effect when inside a pi/form (form context always takes precedence).

variant.description:
Visual style variant of the toggle buttons.
- `"default"` — transparent background, highlights on active.
- `"outline"` — bordered buttons, grouped or spaced.
- `"pill"` — segmented-control style: muted rounded-full container with a   filled foreground pill on the active item.

spacing.description: Gap between toggle buttons (in Tailwind spacing units). `0` = buttons are joined (no gap, rounded ends only). Positive values add space between each button.

disabled.description: When true, the entire group is disabled and non-interactive.

className.description: Extra Tailwind / CSS classes forwarded to the root element.

name.description: Field name used to bind to FormContext when inside a pi/form card. When provided the component reads its value from form state and writes back via form.handleChange.

ReactValue.description: A React-only value (element type, CSS properties, node); free-form JSON here.

columnWidths.description:
Initial column widths. Supports CSS-like values:   - '200px'  — fixed initial width   - '30%'    — explicit percentage   - '1fr'    — fraction of remaining space (after px/% columns)

Defaults to equal split when omitted or when length doesn't match columnCards.

minColumnPercent.description: Minimum percentage any column can shrink to during drag. Default: 10

cells.description: 2D array of cards — cells[row][col]. Must be rectangular (all rows same length).

columnWidths.description:
Initial column widths using CSS-like values:   - '200px'  — fixed initial width (resolved against container width at mount)   - '30%'    — explicit percentage of container   - '1fr'    — fraction of remaining space after px/% columns   - 'auto'   — natural content width; no drag handle rendered for adjacent boundaries

Defaults to equal `1fr` split when omitted.

rowHeights.description:
Initial row heights using the same syntax as columnWidths. 'auto' rows follow content height (max across all cells in that row). No drag handle is rendered between two rows unless both are explicit (non-auto).

Defaults to equal `1fr` split when omitted.

minColumnPercent.description: Minimum percentage any explicit column can shrink to during drag. Default: 10

minRowPercent.description: Minimum percentage any explicit row can shrink to during drag. Default: 10

content.description: Ordered list of panels to render inside the resizable group.

direction.description: Layout direction of the panel group.  Defaults to `"horizontal"`.

handles.description:
Handle configuration(s) between panels.

- A single `PiResizableHandle` is used for every handle in the group.
- An array must have exactly `content.length - 1` entries.

Defaults to  {@link  DefResizableHandle }  (visible drag handle).

style.description:
Optional Shadcn-style style overrides.

When provided as `{ shad?: { root?: string; panel?: string; handle?: string } }`, the nested class names are applied to the corresponding elements in addition to any `className` already set.

ResponsiveCardRef.description:
A card reference that can optionally vary by screen size.

Pass a plain `PiCardRef` string to always show the same card, or a  {@link  SizeMap }  to show different cards (or none) at each breakpoint.

position.description: Pixel offset from the top of the scrollable content. Acts as the start position for range markers.

extent.description:
Length of the annotation in content pixels.

Required when `markerType === "range"`.  The marker will span `[position, position + extent]` in content space.

markerType.description: Shape of the minimap marker.  Defaults to `"point"`.

title.description: Short human-readable label shown in detail views.

description.description: Full description shown when the annotation is selected/inspected.

className.description:
Optional extra CSS class(es) applied to this marker's DOM element.

Use this to style individual annotations differently from the default type-based colour, e.g. to highlight a "selected" annotation:

  className: "swa-selected"

ScrollbarAnnotation.description:
A single annotation marker placed on the scrollbar minimap.

All positions are **pixel offsets from the top of the scrollable content** (i.e. relative to `scrollHeight`).

| markerType | required fields          | |------------|--------------------------| | `"point"`  | `position`               | | `"bar"`    | `position`               | | `"range"`  | `position` + `extent`    |

contentCard.description:
Pihanga card reference for the scrollable main content.

The card is rendered inside the scroll container, so it can be any Pihanga card (plain text, a Plate editor, a list, etc.).

annotations.description: Annotations to display as coloured markers on the scrollbar track.

className.description: Optional additional CSS class applied to the root element.

reportEventsOnScroll.description:
When `true`, `onAnnotationHovered` events are emitted even while the content container is being scrolled.

Defaults to `false` (suppression is the default) to avoid flooding Redux with hover actions as markers pass under the cursor during scroll.

reason.description:
- 'user': dismissed by user (outside click, ESC, X button)
- 'programmatic': closed via props.open change

propagate.description: When `true` the key event is NOT stopped — it propagates normally after the pihanga `onShortcut` event fires.  Default: `false`.

ShortcutDef.description:
A single keyboard shortcut to intercept.

`key` matches `KeyboardEvent.key` (e.g. `"k"`, `"Escape"`, `"ArrowUp"`) or `KeyboardEvent.code` (e.g. `"KeyK"`).

`modifiers` lists the modifier keys that **must** be active; any modifier not listed is expected to be **inactive** (strict matching).

`id` is an optional caller-defined label that is forwarded in the event so you can distinguish shortcuts without pattern-matching on key+modifiers.

`propagate` controls whether the key event continues down the DOM tree after the overlay handles it.  Defaults to `false` (the event is consumed here). Set to `true` to fire the pihanga event **and** still let the browser / focused child element see the keystroke.

SizeT.description:
Shadcn component size token.

Maps directly to the `size` prop accepted by `@/components/ui/button`.

SkeletonRowSize.description:
Named height presets for skeleton rows.

| Value | Height   | Typical use                     | |-------|----------|---------------------------------| | `xs`  | 12 px    | Tiny text / timestamp lines     | | `sm`  | 20 px    | Small text or menu items        | | `md`  | 40 px    | Standard input / row (default)  | | `lg`  | 56 px    | Large card rows                 | | `xl`  | 80 px    | Wide widget / hero section      |

SkeletonSpacing.description:
Named gap presets between skeleton rows.

| Value | Gap    | |-------|--------| | `sm`  |  8 px  | | `md`  | 12 px  | | `lg`  | 16 px  |

divider.description: Optional card ref rendered as a separator between children

spacing.description: Tailwind gap spacing units between children

className.description: Additional Tailwind utility classes

style.description: Card style object (use the `shad` key for Tailwind-compatible overrides)

data.description: Arbitrary data attributes rendered as `data-{key}={value}` on the root element

title.description: Short label shown below/beside the step indicator.

description.description: Optional secondary text shown under the title.

optional.description: If true, an "(Optional)" suffix is appended to the title. Mirrors the MUI Joy UI `optional` prop.

labelCard.description: Optional Pihanga card rendered **instead of** the default title/description text label.  Useful for rich labels (icons, custom markup, etc.). The card receives no extra props — use `memo` in its own declaration if it needs to read from state.

contentCard.description: A card ref rendered as the body of this step when it is active and the stepper is in `"vertical"` orientation with `showContent: true`.

StepItem.description: A single step in the stepper.

activeStep.description:
0-based index of the currently active step (controlled mode). Steps before this index are rendered as "completed"; steps after are "upcoming".

Required in controlled mode (`selfManaged: false`). Used as the initial value in self-managed mode when provided (otherwise defaults to `defaultActiveStep ?? 0`).

defaultActiveStep.description: Initial active step used only in self-managed mode (`selfManaged: true`). Ignored in controlled mode.

selfManaged.description:
When `true`, the component manages its own `activeStep` state internally. Clicking a step immediately advances the indicator without waiting for the host application to update the `activeStep` prop via a reducer. The `onStepClicked` event is still dispatched on each click.

When `false` (default), `activeStep` fully controls the display.

orientation.description:
Layout orientation.
- `"horizontal"` (default): steps flow left-to-right with labels below.
- `"vertical"`: steps stack top-to-bottom with labels/content to the right.

size.description: Visual size of the step indicators.

showContent.description: When `true` and `orientation === "vertical"`, the active step's `contentCard` is rendered inline beneath its label.

className.description: Additional Tailwind classes applied to the root element.

stepId.description: The `id` of the clicked step definition.

content.description: The card to render inside the Suspense boundary. Typically registered with a `__imp_ReactValue__pihanga2_core` component so it can suspend.

fallback.description: Optional card to use as the Suspense fallback. When provided, the built-in skeleton props below are ignored.

rows.description: Number of placeholder rows shown while suspended.

rowSize.description: Named height preset for each shimmer row.

spacing.description: Named gap preset between shimmer rows.

rowClassName.description: Raw Tailwind classes for every shimmer row. When set, takes precedence over `rowSize`.

className.description: Raw Tailwind classes for the outer wrapper `<div>`. When set, takes precedence over `spacing`.

SuspenseProps.description:
Props for the `shad/suspense` card.

Wraps `content` in a React `<Suspense>` boundary so it can suspend independently of its siblings (e.g. when its component is code-split via `__imp_ReactValue__pihanga2_core`).

**Default fallback** — animated shimmer skeleton rows (same as `shad/loading-skeleton`); customise with `rows` / `rowSize` / `spacing`: ```ts registerCard("myApp/editorSection", PiSuspense({   content: "myApp/codeEditor",   rows:    5,   rowSize: "lg", })); ```

**Custom fallback card** — pass any registered card name via `fallback` to replace the built-in skeleton entirely: ```ts registerCard("myApp/graphSection", PiSuspense({   content:  "myApp/graphView",   fallback: "myApp/graphPlaceholder", })); ```

SwimlaneCallKind.description:
How a message travels between lanes.
- `sync`  – request that expects a reply; opens an activity on the target             and automatically creates an *outstanding reply*.
- `async` – message that opens an activity on the target, closed by `done`.
- `event` – fire-and-forget; no activity.

target.description: New hover target, or `null` when the pointer left all targets.

previous.description: Target that was hovered before, if any.

span.description: Span details for the new target (when it refers to a call).

related.description: Calls made while handling the hovered call (its direct children). Their call and reply transitions are highlighted as well.

process.description: For a hovered transition: call id of the caller-side process (activity) that sent the call and receives its reply. That activity is highlighted.

acts.description: Ids of calls currently being handled by this lane (stack order).

SwimlaneLanesSnapshot.description: Lane id → snapshot. A lane missing from the record does not exist (yet).

current.description: Current snapshot (== `post` of the last row).

type.description: `reply` = implied by a sync call; `expect` = announced explicitly.

SwimlanePending.description: A message that is known to be coming.

model.description: The model to render — usually a state selector `(s) => s.swimlane`.

showPending.description: Show outstanding messages below the "now" line. Default `true`.

autoFollow.description: Keep the newest row in view while the user is at the bottom of the scroll container. Scrolling up pauses following. Default `true`.

showTooltip.description: Show the built-in hover tooltip. Default `true`.

highlightId.description: Highlight a call chain (call, activity, reply, outstanding reply) by id, in addition to whatever the pointer is hovering.

laneWidth.description: Horizontal distance between lifelines in px. Default 104.

rowHeight.description: Height of each transition row in px. Default 30.

headerHeight.description: Height of the header holding the vertical lane names. Default 130.

gutterWidth.description: Width of the left timestamp column in px. Default 92.

stickyTop.description: `top` offset for the sticky header (e.g. height of a navbar). Default 0.

now.description: Clock (epoch ms) used for "waiting …" timers and overdue detection of outstanding messages. When omitted the card ticks its own wall clock (4×/s, only while something is outstanding). Pass it to drive the card entirely from props — e.g. for replaying a recorded trace or for tests.

fulfilled.description: Set when this event replaced an outstanding (expected) message.

route.description: For `reply` / `done` rows: the originating call, resolved at ingest time so the row stays drawable after its span has been garbage-collected.

SwimlaneRow.description: One rendered transition. `pre` / `post` are the lane snapshots before and after the event: the top half of the row is drawn from `pre`, the bottom half from `post`.

ts.description: Epoch ms. Defaults to `Date.now()` at ingest time.

fulfils.description: Id of an `expect` event that this real event resolves.

timeoutMs.description: For `sync`: when the expected reply becomes overdue (ms after `ts`).

parentId.description: Id of the call whose processing caused this call (like a trace's parent span id). When omitted it is inferred at ingest time as the innermost activity open on the `from` lane — exact for sequential processing, a best guess when one service handles several requests concurrently.

parent.description: Call whose processing caused this one (explicit `parentId` or inferred).

value.description: Controlled: the currently active tab id. Must be provided (or supplied via a state mapper) when selfManaged is false (the default).

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled initial active tab id. Used as the initial value in self-managed mode when value is not set; falls back to the first tab id if omitted.

When true, the component manages its own active tab state internally. The onTabChanged event is still dispatched on every change so external reducers can observe the selection.

Maximum number of tabs to display as a standard tab strip. When the number of tabs exceeds this value the tab selector is replaced by a drop-down `<Select>` menu while the tab content area continues to work as normal.

When omitted (or `undefined`) the tab strip is always used regardless of how many tabs there are.
